newsitem.title: LEBANON: Lebanon says army detained disappeared Jordanian.
newsitem.headline: Lebanon says army detained disappeared Jordanian.

text.p: Lebanon's prosecutor general said on Tuesday a Jordanian executive of a Beirut hotel who disappeared on January 3 had been detained on the orders of Lebanese military authorities.

But prosecutor Adnan Addoum declined to confirm the whereabouts of Derar al-Karmi, financial controller at the Marriott Hotel. Jordanian Ambassador Fakhry Abou Taleb has indicated that he was being held by Syrian security forces.
"Derar al-Karmi was detained by orders of the military prosecutor general," Addoum, who had previously denied all knowledge of the case and refused to comment on it, told reporters.
Asked why Karmi, a longtime Marriott employee, was being held, he said: "I do not wish to comment on this issue."
Beirut newspapers have said Karmi is being held on suspicion of links with recent anti-Syrian attacks in Lebanon and Syria.

Asked if he was being held in Lebanon, Addoum said: "I refuse to confirm or deny this." Some Beirut newspapers said he was being held in Syria, which has 35,000 troops in Lebanon and is the country's main power broker.

Abou Taleb, the Jordanian ambassador, said on Monday that Karmi, who is of Palestinian origin, was being held by non-Lebanese security forces "concerned with Lebanese security", an apparent reference to Syria.

Newspapers have reported that he was being questioned over a December 18 machinegun attack on a van carrying Syrian workers in a Christian area north of Beirut in which the driver was killed, or about a December 31 bus bombing in Damascus that killed 11 people.
